p116018.body:
## Piece 24: [Effort ledger][24-29] feat(runtime): the effort predictor registers its picks with the pod's StartedPicks

Re-cut piece P24 of the [Effort ledger] series (map: PIECES-20261111.md). New PR.

Part of #107264 / Design #107997 §2.1 / Umbrella #94912

Observed vs inferred: observed — head 9c59354b (north-star commit 35 on base 3402f1c7).
- On P23 the predictor can register starts, but nothing hands it the pod's StartedPicks: build_processor_worker builds the predictor from the signal router's turn history and the metadata store only.
- The same patch, cut writer-free on lane F (3e621fab), passed check-ni 6765. The router test passed gate-ext 6391 (aether_routing:started_picks, 1/1).
- The runtime tests have no band lane since L3, and the band is blocked on Rust 1.96, so the Aether Rust PR Pipeline on this head is their verdict.

Inferred: none.

Contract relied on: EffortPredictor::with_started_picks (P23) and StartedPicks (P3). The pod TurnHistory and the summary store stay wired as before.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): holds. No ask moves; the production binding of the predictor's start registration is deferred to #116019.

Invariant 2 (commit before send): not in this piece; it lives whole in P22. There is no record write and no forwarding here.

What changes:
- SignalRouter::with_started_picks and started_picks, both documented, let the router carry the pod's StartedPicks.
- build_effort_predictor binds a StartedPicks to the predictor when it is given one.
- The production binding is deferred to #116019 (the consumer): in this PR build_signal_router creates no StartedPicks and build_processor_worker passes None, so no start is registered in production until the egress that takes the starts ships with it (3f608d86).

Mutants killed:
- The builder arm dropping the picks (`Some(_picks) => predictor`): the_root_hands_the_effort_predictor_the_pods_started_picks (tier3_app_telemetry). It was submitted as a revert-red run; that run was cancelled when TP moved, so this mutant is reasoned, not executed.
- The setter dropping the picks, or the getter answering another registry: the_router_hands_back_the_started_picks_it_binds (signal_router_tests).

Open item recorded (FIDO review 292935546): effort_stamp.rs:316, the turnless build reads the unsent mark apart from the state. Unreachable while PROXY_OWNS_HISTORY is false; tracked in the post-live backlog under #128103.

Overlap (open PRs, 11-11 ~18Z, `gh pr list --search effort`): bootstrap.rs is also touched by Chiqun #109247 (the effort-history writer, open, not draft; not stacked on, D-20261111-9) and by #90704 (crate split; also tier3_app_telemetry.rs). signal_router.rs: none. Based on main, on no Chiqun PR.

## Evidence

Peer: architect review approved at 56be9b24; Ken peer review approved at 56be9b24 (https://microsoft.ghe.com/bic/aether/pull/116018#issuecomment-293627386); yugo rules all three items not blocking at 56be9b24 (https://microsoft.ghe.com/bic/aether/pull/116018#issuecomment-293630301).
Tests: a remote build of 56be9b24 (full-workspace clippy, the PR pipeline lint replica, ADO run 192097779): red only in files this PR does not change, all also red on main (aether_hive respond_card_tests.rs:472, aether_middleware jwt_auth.rs:1676, aether_services cold_home_list_tests.rs:4483).
CI: GitHub checks at 56be9b24: 7 passed, 1 failed; the failed Aether Rust PR Pipeline (buildId=192089995) is red only on breaks main fixed after its merge ref (#130972, #130970, #130846), none in a file this PR changes.
Banana premerge: not run at 56be9b24.
Human hold: none. The automaton's changes-requested review under lukas at c1b43ad5 was dismissed as stale: its items are fixed at 56be9b24 or tracked as sub-issues of #127551.

Written by [figaro](https://github.com/jack-work/figaro) 0.71.1 (claude-opus-5.5) on behalf of John Kelliher.

## Piece 25: [Effort ledger][25-29] feat(effort): the effort ledger marks a tier the CLI was never sent; one ownership predicate per entry

Re-cut piece P25 of the [Effort ledger] series (map: PIECES-20261111.md). New PR.

Part of #107264 / Design #107997 §2.2 / Umbrella #94912

Observed vs inferred: observed — head e860ff6e (north-star commits 36-37 on base 3402f1c7). gate-kit 6502 (aether_contracts_actors) passed on the same two patches at eecb2b76, and check-ni 6779 passed at b2c5bce2 (patch-identical, range-diff `=`). inferred — nothing reads the mark or the predicate until P26, so production behaviour is unchanged here.

Contract relied on: `EffortLedger::persisting_port` (main, #108259): a clear goes through the attached port live or not, an effort through a live one; `takes_history_items` (P1), ours.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): not touched; no ask here.

Invariant 2 (commit before send): not in this piece; it lives whole in P22. No record write, no forwarding.

What changes:
- EffortLedger keeps an unsent mark beside its state. TurnEffort::write_stamp takes `unsent`. An unsent tier is never persisted; one written over a persisted tier persists a clear through `persisting_port`; a block's put-back restores the mark it replaced. Every production caller passes `false` here.
- EffortStarter::proxy_owns_history (default false) and TurnEffort::proxy_owned: the starter claims the wire, the entry takes history items, and the router reads live.
- effort_stamp's ledger write moves into `hold()`, which takes the unsent mark.

Tests (each fails on revert of its mechanism): an_unsent_hold_is_never_persisted_and_clears_a_persisted_tier; proxy_owned_needs_the_claim_an_in_history_entry_and_a_live_router; main's a_clear_put_back_or_written_off_the_switch_is_persisted still holds over the merged replace/restore_if.

Overlap (open PRs on the same files, 11-11; based on main, stacked on none): effort_prediction.rs: Chiqun #110764, #110166, #111118; ours #111569, #110136, #110266, #110267.

In mode off the CLI also applies a client tier (the stamp cannot see the record); with entries both carry the same tier.

## Piece 26: [Effort ledger][26-29] feat(effort): the stamp sends no tier on a proxy-owned entry; the effort predictor leaves the entry to the LLM proxy

Re-cut piece P26 of the [Effort ledger] series (map: PIECES-20261111.md). New PR.

Part of #107264 / Design #107997 §2.2 / Umbrella #94912

Observed vs inferred: observed — head 0e4e3bea (north-star commits 38-39 on base 3402f1c7). gate-ext 6767 (aether_grpc:effort_stamp) passed at b2c5bce2 and check-ni 6779 there, on patches identical to these (range-diff `=`). Staged: at this piece `effort_predictor::PROXY_OWNS_HISTORY` is `false`, so every tier stays on the wire and the CLI is still told the turn's tier (test `before_the_seat_binds_a_client_tier_stays_on_the_wire`). Inferred, once a later piece binds the proxy's seat and flips the switch: with `aether.reasoning_effort_mode` live, a turn on an in-history entry gets no tier from the stamp and its effort comes from the LLM proxy's record (P16-P22) fed by the registered pick (P23-P24).

Contract relied on: the container and the engine call `setReasoningEffort` only when the stamped ModelInfo effort moves (engine_serve `apply_effort_change`, `ModelTransition::EffortOnly`), theirs; P25's mark and predicate, ours.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): holds; the stamp and the predictor's ownership claim ask nothing at the egress.

Invariant 2 (commit before send): not in this piece; it lives whole in P22. The stamp writes the pod ledger only, never the record.

What changes:
- On a proxy-owned entry the stamp sends no tier, a client's own included (one author): the container and the engine call no setReasoningEffort there.
- A landed pick the entry runs at, on the turn's host, is held on the ledger unsent for the predictor's overlay, never stepped; a turnless build serves the catalog default over an unsent tier. The apply row reads outcome=proxy_owned path=proxy_owned; 2026-10-23-reasoning-effort-live.md names it.
- EffortPredictor's turn answers proxy_owns_history true.

Size: 479 lines, 50 code / 429 tests (test-heavy, option (a)).

Tests (effort_stamp_tests, each fails on revert of its arm): a_proxy_owned_entry_is_never_stamped_with_a_predicted_tier, a_proxy_owned_entry_is_not_stepped, a_turnless_build_never_serves_a_tier_the_proxy_holds, a_proxy_hold_over_a_persisted_tier_clears_the_store, a_block_puts_back_what_a_proxy_owned_hold_replaced, a_restored_ledger_never_holds_a_tier_the_proxy_held, a_proxy_owned_hold_refuses_another_host_release, a_proxy_owned_hold_refuses_an_unsupported_pick, proxy_owned_needs_the_entry_and_a_live_router; effort_predictor_tests: the_effort_predictor_leaves_an_in_history_entry_to_the_llm_proxy.

Overlap (open PRs on the same files, 11-11; based on main, stacked on none): effort_stamp.rs / effort_stamp_tests.rs / effort_predictor.rs / 2026-10-23-reasoning-effort-live.md: Chiqun #110764, #110166, #111118; ours #111569, #111623, #108654, #108669, #108677, #108680, #108718, #108719, #109349.

In mode off the CLI also applies a client tier (the stamp cannot see the record); with entries both carry the same tier.

Fixes #127551

## 🔴 Automaton Review: Request Changes

**PR #116018** | 23 files changed | 13 reviewers · 4 models | 20 findings | 85% consensus
*Multi-reviewer agreement: 17/20 findings confirmed by 2+ reviewers*

The PR wires the effort predictor into the pod's StartedPicks and adds dormant P25/P26 ownership machinery. Ledger write races, an under-specified design doc and weak registry tests need to be fixed before PROXY_OWNS_HISTORY flips or AppliedEfforts is bound.


*This change touches the reasoning-effort ledger pipeline. The effort predictor (aether_services) now registers MD1 starts with the pod-local StartedPicks registry, which is bound in the aether_runtime composition root and evicted at deactivation. The EffortLedger gains an unsent mark, the stamp (aether_grpc) gains a proxy-ownership arm, and a new AppliedEfforts register lets proxy egress record applied tiers. Everything new is gated behind PROXY_OWNS_HISTORY=false or the unbound AppliedEfforts register, so the change is backward-compatible and rolling-safe. The one exception is the StartedPicks producer, which is bound now and relies on #116019 landing its consumer back to back, especially in live mode.*

### What's Good

- The core unsent-persistence tests hard-code expected values, include sent-tier controls and name the mutants they kill.
- The ordinary ECS-precedence defect is fixed via ecs_serves, with a regression test, and the stale StartedPicks producer/teardown rustdoc is corrected.
- The new registers use Weak handles

🔴 **Changes requested by automaton**, submitted under `lukas`'s credential on the owner's behalf so the block counts toward this repository's merge rules. No person reviewed this change; the findings are in [automaton's review](https://microsoft.ghe.com/bic/aether/pull/116018#pullrequestreview-234338191) and its inline comments. automaton withdraws this block itself when a later review approves, or when its findings are dealt with on a newer commit.

p131611.title: [Security Judge MD1][5-10] feat(security-judge): the MD1 compare record and its counter
p131611.body:
Fixes #130984
Part of #130874

## Intent

When the Security Judge is later compared with the decision model MD1, each compared judgment needs one comparison record and a count of how the comparisons turned out. This change adds the shape of that record and of that count, ready for a later piece to fill in. Nothing writes either yet, so nothing changes for anyone until the comparison is switched on. The record holds codes, sizes, timings and probabilities only, never anything a user or a tool wrote. It is internal telemetry, the same for every audience.

Example: a compared judgment where MD1 and the final verdict both allowed writes one `md1_compare` record with `md1_outcome=agreed`, `md1_reason=decided`, MD1's four answers with their probabilities, and one count of `orchestrator_security_judge_md1_compare_total{outcome=agreed, reason=decided}`. A judgment MD1 was never asked about writes `md1_outcome=not_compared` and its skip reason, with no answer keys.

Comments on the issue since the claim: the run's own status comment and the miner's advisory (other open pulls sharing `telemetry.rs` and `metrics.txt`, listed under Nearby work). Neither changes the ask.

## Scope

**In scope**
- `JudgeEvent::Md1Compare`: a Rust-only `phase=md1_compare` log record, every field named, with its sink arm, its place in `every_log_event` and the key pin.
- `JudgeEvent::Md1CompareCounter` and `orchestrator_security_judge_md1_compare_total{outcome,reason}` with its `MetricSpec`, and the one `docs/protocol/metrics.txt` line as its own commit.
- Tests that pin the record's exact keys and values, that no row carries text, the counter's label rows and the closed reason set.

**Out of scope**
- Anything that produces the record or the count: piece 6 (#130985). Nothing in production constructs either event.
- The ECS keys and the MD1 port (piece 4, #130982), the state-token field (piece 9) and any ECS rule: they belong to other pieces, and every piece ships switched off.
- Not requested: a Python twin, a Kusto query over the record (piece 10, #130989 captures it), or a second sink arm that increments the counter itself.

## Grounding

- The shape follows the existing log-and-counter pairs in `aether_rust/crates/aether_services/src/security_judge/telemetry.rs` (`Verdict` with `VerdictCounter`). The record is boxed like `Verdict`. `Md1CompareLine` derives no `Default`, so a producer names every field.
- Every value on a row is a `&'static str`, a closed enum, a number, or `log_token(model)`, so no request text can reach a field. A test enforces it.
- Saved queries read `attributes.fields`, as `dashboards/kusto/security_judge_stand_in_fail_open.kql` does, so the Kusto allowlist is not edited.
- The counter has its own event, not an increment inside the record's sink arm. Every other judge counter is its own event, and the `Records` test sinks would otherwise never see it. The sink's spec match has an explicit arm ahead of the `_ => &FAIL_OPEN_TOTAL` fall-through, so the increment is not booked as fail-open. `outcome` joins `COUNTER_LABEL_KEYS`.
- The reason lives inside the outcome: `Md1CompareOutcome::NotCompared(&'static str)`. `reason()` is the one source for the record's `md1_reason` and the counter's `reason`, so the two cannot disagree. A compared row can only read `decided`, and a not-compared row never does. Rejected: a separate `reason` field, which would leave the pairing to every producer.
- The message is the fixed literal `security_judge | md1 compare`, and every value rides a named field. The design asked for an interpolated line with the values in it, but `no_new_interpolation_into_tracing_message_position` refuses a new interpolated message site, and the rust-coding standard allows one only for a Python-parity message, which this record has none. Rejected: a baseline row (grows a shrink-only ledger), and writing the `key={}` tokens in the macro literal (the record and the sink would each format one line).
- Probabilities are written as typed `f64` and sizes as typed `u64`, so `attributes.fields` holds numbers. `record()` renders them with `{:?}` and `to_string()`, which is how the key pin reads them back.
- The reason list is a copy: `MD1_NOT_COMPARED_REASONS` repeats the admission skips and the shared MD1 design's `Md1Miss` spellings, and `Md1Miss` does not exist yet (piece 4). The reason test pins the list to the counter's description in both directions. Piece 6 owes the test that every `Md1Miss::as_str` is on the list.
- Answer keys are spelled `md1_<question>` and `md1_<question>_prob`, and a compared row's `md1_reason` reads `decided`. The request names neither; the shared design's `md1_live` uses the same word.

Observed vs inferred: observed — the row, key, no-text and counter tests and the tracing-message source lint ran on this head (see How to verify); nothing emits the record, checked with `git grep Md1Compare`.
Contract relied on: the confirmed request on #130984 and its parent #130874 for the keys and label sets; `docs/protocol/metrics.txt` and `source_lints` `metrics_txt_registry` for the metric name; `source_lints` `no_new_interpolation_into_tracing_message_position` and its baseline for the message.

## Nearby work

- #131601 (`ponia/md1-decision-state-once`, piece 3, same stack): shares `security_judge/telemetry.rs`. It adds verdict keys and this change adds new items and one `every_log_event` entry, touching no line of its verdict keys. Whichever lands second merges main.
- #131607 (`mike/be95-revert-118493`) and #131512 (`norbert/635a-revert-batch-d`): share `docs/protocol/metrics.txt`, a union-merged file. This change adds one line; a clean merge there is re-read for a name the other side deleted.
- Board claim for piece 3: https://microsoft.ghe.com/bic/aether/discussions/131038 (decision state built once), same file as #131601.
- This run's board claim: https://microsoft.ghe.com/bic/aether/discussions/131057.
- Five older open pulls edit `telemetry.rs`, mostly verdict keys (#125755, #122437, #122391, #124182, #123181). This change leaves `RUST_ONLY_VERDICT_KEYS` alone; the merge gate checks the merged tree.

## Changes

- `aether_rust/crates/aether_services/src/security_judge/telemetry.rs`: the two variants, `Md1CompareOutcome`, `Md1Answer`, `Md1CompareLine`, `MD1_COMPARE_TOTAL`, the reason lists, the `record()` and sink arms, `outcome` in `COUNTER_LABEL_KEYS`, and the tests: the key and value pins, the reason set, the `every_log_event` entry and the counter-keys test.
- `aether_rust/crates/aether_services/src/security_judge/telemetry_counter_tests.rs`: three MD1 emits (`agreed`, `not_compared` with `dropped`, `not_compared` with an unknown reason reading `other`) and their expected rows.
- `docs/protocol/metrics.txt`: the line `orchestrator_security_judge_md1_compare_total`, in its own commit.

## How to verify

From `aether_rust/`, each with its output sent to a file:

- `cargo nextest run -p aether_services --lib -E 'test(/security_judge::telemetry/)'` should show 10 passed, the two MD1 tests and the counter test among them.
- `cargo nextest run -p source_lints --lib -E 'test(no_new_interpolation_into_tracing_message_position)'` should pass with `tracing_message_interpolation.baseline.txt` unchanged.
- `cargo clippy -p aether_services --all-targets -- -D warnings` should pass.
- `git grep Md1Compare` should find only the two Rust files and `docs/protocol/metrics.txt`, so a mode-off evaluation writes nothing new.

Not run: the full `aether_services` and `source_lints` suites and the merged-tree check against current main; CI and the merge gate's premerge run them.

## Follow-ups

- The row test cannot tell `fast_decision` from MD1's decision: the one fixture that sets both gives them `allow`. A third row with the fast stage blocking and no MD1 decision closes it. This change or piece 6 (#130985), which adds the first producer, carries it.
- Piece 6 owes the pin that every `Md1Miss::as_str` is on `MD1_NOT_COMPARED_REASONS`.

## Reviews

- code_review: APPROVED, at `39b37d84ea91`.
- deep_challenge: APPROVED, one non-blocking minor (the `fast_decision` pin above).
- prompt_review: APPROVED, no model-facing text in the diff.
- unit_test_verify: PASS (the telemetry tests, the tracing-message lint and a further source lint, all exit 0).
- user_journey_verify: PASS, 3 traced, 0 ran. These were traced through the code only.

p130950.title: feat(effort-router): ask on a conversation's first turn whatever the cache-safe list says
p130950.body:
Fixes #130206

## Intent

The effort router decides how hard the assistant thinks about a message, but only on models where changing that mid-chat is known not to lose the chat's saved context. That check also ran on a chat's first message, where nothing is saved yet, so chats on models outside the measured list were never routed. After this change, a chat's first message on a model the router has a reading for (its own trained row, for example `gpt-6.1-terra`, or, since #130734, the pooled fallback row for a model that offers `medium` and `high`) is routed whatever the list says, unless the model's current effort is above `high` (the router only picks `medium` or `high`, so any pick would lower it for the whole chat), and a live router keeps that effort for the chat's later messages. Later messages still go through the check, no model is added to the list, and there is no new switch: the router's existing mode decides.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[identity, trained row] --> B{cache_risk}
  B -->|completions_wire / host_not_in_history| OFF[off]
  B -->|pair unlisted| T{PromptTurn}
  T -->|Later| OFF2[off: model_not_in_history; ledger keeps the tier]
  T -->|"First (new)"| H{current tier above high?}
  H -->|yes| OFF5[off: model_not_in_history]
  H -->|no| X{tokens leg?}
  B -->|pair listed| P{handed modelId = listed?}
  P -->|no| OFF3[off: profile_not_in_history]
  P -->|yes| X
  X -->|yes| OFF4[off: transport_no_in_history]
  X -->|no| ON[ECS mode: shadow or live]
```

Before this change an unlisted pair went straight to `model_not_in_history` on every turn.

Example: on `gpt-6.1-terra`, a chat that opens with a hard analysis question runs at high effort throughout when the router is live; one that opens with a greeting keeps medium.

## Scope

In scope:
- A first turn on an entry that `IN_HISTORY` does not list and that has a reading (its own row, or the pooled fallback row #130734 added) is asked, and its pick is recorded (shadow) or applied (live). An entry whose current tier ranks above `high` is not asked: the router picks only `medium` or `high`, so any pick would lower it, and the ledger would hold the lower tier for the conversation.
- Later turns on that entry are not routed and serve the held first-turn tier from the ledger.
- The live stamp stops refusing an unlisted pair on its own turn position, and keeps one only where the conversation's ledger already holds a tier for the entry (a lost-count message). The design record and rustdoc say so.

Out of scope:
- Widening `IN_HISTORY`: the owner called it an infra change.
- Fallback rows for models with no trained row: #130167, merged as #130734. Combined with this change, first turns on unlisted entries that read the fallback row are routed too, except those running above `high`; main's fallback record (`2026-11-18-reasoning-effort-fallback-rows.md`) names #130206 as the change that would open them.
- Any ECS key, flight or config: the owner asked for none.
- Exempting `transport_no_in_history`, `profile_not_in_history` on a listed pair, `completions_wire` or `host_not_in_history` on a first turn. Each is a delivery precondition or "a first turn on a listed model behaves as today" (see Grounding). Not requested: widening the exemption to them.

## Grounding

- The measured loss is a mid-conversation effort change dropping the messages cache (Opus 5.5 on MSIT, 2026-11-03/04). A first turn has no cached messages. Contract: `aether_rust/docs/design/2026-10-23-reasoning-effort-live.md` §3.2 (gates and ledger) and §3.5 (limits), both amended here.
- `cache_risk` and `operating_mode` in `aether_rust/crates/aether_services/src/decision_judge/effort_predictor.rs` take a `PromptTurn`. Both production callers, `BoundTurn::asking_mode` and `BoundTurn::start_at`, pass `PromptTurn::of_ordinal(..)`, the read `ready` already uses to pick the first-turn prompt. So the hold, the early start, the start and the prompt choice rest on one read.
- `cli_identity_off_history` in `aether_rust/crates/aether_grpc/src/effort_stamp.rs` loses its unconditional unlisted-pair arm. That arm was added by #95162 on the note "the dispatch never starts one live". On a first turn the premise now fails by design. The function now takes `holds_tier` (`same_entry && state.effort.is_some()`, from `decide`'s one ledger read) and keeps an unlisted pair as `model_not_in_history` when the ledger already holds a tier for the entry; an empty ledger applies. A later turn's plan on an unlisted pair is off with `model_not_in_history`, so the stamp's decision is not reached for it, and `TurnEffort::applies_to` runs just before the check and refuses unless the build's (entry, release) equals the pair the start judged (`started_on`). A listed pair handed another `modelId` is still kept as `profile_not_in_history`.
- Above `high`: `cache_risk` keeps an unlisted pair off (`model_not_in_history`) on a first turn when the served current tier ranks above every class the first-turn router picks (`above_first_turn_classes`, over `effort_router::CLASSES`). Without it, a first turn on an `xhigh`-default entry with no row of its own (`gpt-5.5`, `gpt-5.6-terra`) would be asked, `step_toward` would move it from `xhigh` to `high` for either pick, and the ledger would hold `high` for the conversation. The stamp is unchanged: an off plan never reaches it. A pick can still lower an entry that opens at `high` on an off-list model, or a cache-safe entry an overlay raises above `medium`; the fallback-rows record §6 names both.
- Later turns need no new code: `ledger_stamp` serves the held tier and reads no list. The one other reader of the list is `takes_history_items`, read by `history_effort_seat` (`with_history_effort` has no non-test caller) and, since #116018, by `TurnEffort::proxy_owned` and `proxy_writes_client_tier`, which decide who owns an entry's effort (`PROXY_OWNS_HISTORY` is false in production). For an unlisted entry it answers false, so the entry stays the stamp's and the stamp applies a first-turn pick itself (`effort_stamp_proxy_tests::proxy_owned_needs_the_entry_and_a_live_router`); the `IN_HISTORY` rustdoc says so.
- Reasons a first turn still honours, and why:
  - `completions_wire`: a delivery limit, since the chat-completions egress never sends the CLI's effort.
  - `host_not_in_history`: with no release, `applies_to` refuses at the stamp anyway, so exempting it would buy a 300 ms hold that applies nothing.
  - `transport_no_in_history`: a first-turn pick on the tokens leg is unmeasured.
  - `profile_not_in_history` on a listed pair: the owner's line "a first turn on a model already on the list behaves as today".
- Rejected alternatives: exempting all three list reasons (needs a first-turn read in the stamp, a new `EffortStarter::first_turn` defaulted across 32 test doubles, and departs from the listed-model line); a `first_turn` field on `EffortPlan` (struct literals across three crates, and `applies_to` already binds the pair); a stamp-side first-turn flag on the plan (it would come from the same ordinal read that picks the plan, so it would not catch a lost count); filtering `model_not_in_history` out of `operating_mode`'s result (`cache_risk` returns before the transport check, so an unlisted tokens-leg first turn would be routed unchecked); telling a first turn by an empty history (a second read that can disagree with the one that picks the prompt); adding terra to `IN_HISTORY` (out of scope).
- Who is affected at deploy: first-turn `predict` rows that read `model_not_in_history` in the design's production query (US, 6 h, `CSCAnalytics`, not re-run here): `gpt-6.1-sol-substrate` 1,189, `opus-5.5-fast` 783 (14 of them live), `gpt-6.1-sol-fast` 14, `gpt-6.1-terra` 0. Where the router mode is `live`, those entries start being routed when this deploys. Since #130734 merged, so do first turns on unlisted entries with no row of their own that offer `medium` and `high` and run at or below `high`: before it they read `untrained_model`, so these counts do not include them. In shadow (the fleet default) and live alike, these entries' first turns now ask Microsoft-Decision-1 (1,986 rows per 6 h by the same counts, against 272,299 conversations with a first-turn row), and an optimistic turn's ask goes out before its DLP verdict; only live applies the pick.
- Rollback: the mode (`aether.reasoning_effort_mode`) is the deciding read. Flipping it to shadow or off drops a held tier at the next build that runs the stamp (design §3.2 Ledger), which is one mid-conversation change for a chat on such an entry, on a pair not measured for in-history delivery, so it can cost a cache rewrite (the design's Rollback bullet and the mode's Rollback cell in `reasoning-effort-prediction.md` say so). A code revert drops nothing, because `ledger_stamp` reads no list.
- Lost message count: a mid-conversation message that reads ordinal 1 after a lost count is asked as a first turn on an unlisted entry, once. The stamp keeps its pick (`model_not_in_history`) when the conversation's ledger already holds a tier for the entry, whether its first turn moved one or a live restore returned it. A live ledger holds no tier after a first turn served at the catalog default and after a rollback of the mode that cleared the stored copy and then read live again, so a lost count there can still move one tier, once; the design records both as accepted residuals. Such a message is still planned live, because `cache_risk` reads the turn's position and no ledger: on a conversation whose ledger holds a tier, it pays the judge call, the dispatch waits up to `LIVE_DEADLINE`, its predict row reads `decided` and its apply row reads `kept` (`model_not_in_history`). In the design's 6 h query, 272,299 conversations had a first-turn row, 8 had two or more, and 5 had a first-turn row after a later one; §3.5 "Lost message count" records it.
- Cut restore: when the first live dispatch after a reactivation cannot restore the stored pair (`phase=applied_restore` outcome `read_failed`, `read_lost`, `read_malformed` or `read_timeout`), it goes ahead with an empty ledger; the next turn, which is not routed, serves the catalog default, and a later dispatch whose read lands brings the held tier back. That is up to two mid-conversation changes on the pair, and nothing in code prevents them; design §3.5 "Unlisted entry" records it.

## Summary

Adds the aux-side M2 ports from the aether_services cut plan (§4 rows 64-70, §7 item 3) and switches their callers. No behaviour changes.

- aether_domain adds two ports to `services::decision_judge`: `LatestAskClip` and `ReasoningEffortRead`.
- `AuxCallPort` gains reply accounting: `AuxPassthroughReply.accounting`, `record_token_usage` and `record_completion`.
- In aether_services, `DecisionText` implements both text ports over the private clip, `TRIM_MARKER` and `reasoning_effort`. Parity tests check that it cuts the same bytes as before.
- Reflection takes the clip, the effort read and the accounting through these ports, so its non-test code no longer reaches into aux modules.
- Memory's instruction gate holds `Arc<dyn DecisionJudgePort>`, tested with a crate-private double.
- aether_runtime binds one `DecisionText` and casts memory's judge to the port.
- New design record: `2026-11-04-aether-services-aux-side-m2-ports.md`. The cut plan is updated.

Already landed elsewhere:
- the type home, now `services::message_text`, in #73367;
- skills' `DecisionJudgePort`, in #105916.

Still open:
- skills' routed call (72af82d3);
- `HomePromptAux` (cb892e62).

p116015.body:
## Piece 17: [Effort ledger][17-29] feat(llm-handler): the effort record seat reads the store on a turn's first call, writes off the call path, and a superseded write adopts the held copy

Part of #107264 / Design #108984 / Umbrella #94912

Deps: P16. Draft until Marius OKs #108984 and the Boss says yes.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): holds; nothing here asks. Invariant 2 (no body is sent from an uncommitted record): holds; this piece builds no body from the record.

Observed vs inferred: observed — the store half of the north star's TE unit 1, cut from it with no change but the superseded write's adopt, which the next piece adds (until then a superseded write is not retried and the pod keeps its copy); its test drives the seat over a store double. The mutant list is reasoned against the test, not executed. Inferred: nothing calls the seat yet, so no pod behaviour changes.

Observed vs inferred: observed — the adopt half of the north star's TE unit 1, unchanged; with it the seat is the north star's unit 1 exactly. The mutant list is reasoned against the test, not executed. Inferred: nothing calls the seat yet, so no pod behaviour changes.

Contract relied on: history_effort::resolve (lane B) takes the newer seq between the pod's copy and the store, a tie to the store; aether_observability::spawn_monitored runs the write with no caller await.

Contract relied on: HistoryEffortStore::write (lane C) answers Superseded when the store holds a copy at a seq at or past the write's; history_effort::resolve gives a tie to the store.

held(): a later call of a turn reads the pod's copy only; a turn's first call also reads the store within 150 ms and takes the newer copy; a read that times out or fails names itself and the call goes as sent. keep() writes a changed record to the store off the call path (a failed write is a WARN) and never an unchanged one.

A write the store supersedes re-reads the store and, when the pod still holds the conversation, takes the newer copy, so the turn's later call reads the winner from memory; one write_refused WARN names the lost and held seqs and whether it adopted; never retried.

Mutants killed:
- a new turn served from memory without the store read, the older copy taken, or an unchanged record written: a_new_turn_reads_the_store_and_takes_the_newer_copy
- a superseded write ignored (the loser keeps its copy), retried, or rowed without its seqs: a_superseded_write_adopts_the_held_record


## Piece 18: [Effort ledger][18-29] feat(llm-handler): the LLM handler holds the effort record seat and the started picks

Part of #107264 / Design #108984 / Umbrella #94912

Deps: P17 and P3 (lane F StartedPicks). Draft until Marius OKs #108984 and the Boss says yes.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): holds; nothing here asks. Invariant 2 (no body is sent from an uncommitted record): holds; this piece builds no body from the record.

Observed vs inferred: observed — the handler half of the north star's TE unit 2, unchanged; the binding test is new. The mutant list is reasoned against the tests, not executed. Inferred: the composition root binds neither yet (lane TG does), and the mode read and the picks have no reader until ledger-te-2c (dead-code expectations), so no pod behaviour changes.

Contract relied on: KvHistoryEffortStore (lane C) is the store over a StringKv; StartedPicks (lane F); the identity peek and get_config_value_raw_for_identity read aether.reasoning_effort_mode as the effort router reads it.

LlmHandler: with_history_effort binds the seat over KvHistoryEffortStore in a StringKv (the store module's dead-code expectation goes: this constructs it); forget_history drops the seat's copy with the rest of the conversation's pod state; with_started_picks binds the picks; history_effort_mode reads aether.reasoning_effort_mode for the call's identity (mode_of: off unless it names a mode).

Mutants killed:
- the binding dropped, or the teardown leaving the seat's copy: the_handler_binds_the_seat_and_forgets_it_with_the_history
- a mode read as on from anything but `shadow`/`live`: the_mode_reads_off_unless_delivered

Overlap (D-20261111-9 census): llm_handler/handler.rs is also touched by Akshay #89572 (draft, conflicts textually; old base) and our #108418 (draft, merges clean); types.rs by #108418 (clean).


Stacked on P17 (#110318). Until #110266/#110267 land, this diff also shows their lines (P18 needs P3's StartedPicks).

## Piece 19: [Effort ledger][19-29] feat(llm-handler): a main-lane call's effort facts and the tier its turn's proposal writes

Part of #107264 / Design #108984 / Umbrella #94912

Deps: P18 (and lane F P1 #110136 for Proposal::tier_for). Draft until Marius OKs #108984 and the Boss says yes.

Invariant 1 (the egress never asks): holds; nothing here asks. Invariant 2 (no body is sent from an uncommitted record): holds; this piece builds no body from the record.

Observed vs inferred: observed — the call-facts part of the north star's TE unit 2, unchanged; its direct tests are new, and the served-tier rows (opus on #110136) ride here. The mutant list is reasoned against the tests, not executed. Inferred: nothing calls these until ledger-te-2c (dead-code expectation), so no pod behaviour changes.

Contract relied on: EffortProposal::resolve and Proposal::tier_for (lane F) answer the tier the egress writes or why none, with the egress cap on EgressCall; reasoning_effort::decide_effort_cap is that cap; takes_history_items (lane F) names the entries measured to take history items.

EffortCall: the facts one main-lane call needs from its arm. eligible: only a body with a request-level effort, on an entry that takes history items, never a responses continuation. resolve_proposal: the turn's proposal resolved and applied through tier_for with decide_effort_cap, `none` without one, its own wait timed. proposal_outcome: what the record holds for the proposal (none, in_force, capped_out, missed, would_commit, committed, dropped). Docs: the live record lists discarded_on_block beside judge_*; the tier-list census names effort_prediction's copy and its pin.

Mutants killed:
- any eligibility check dropped: a_call_is_eligible_with_an_effort_an_in_history_entry_and_no_continuation
- the cap skipped, or no proposal resolving to a tier: the_proposal_resolves_through_the_served_entrys_cap
- an outcome arm dropped or reordered: the_proposal_outcome_names_what_the_record_holds
- the served tier compared or written raw: the_served_tier_is_compared_and_written_trimmed_and_lowercased

Overlap (D-20261111-9 census, 11-11 ~19Z, against P22 80c80469): aether_rust/docs/design/2026-10-23-reasoning-effort-live.md conflicts textually with Chiqun #109247 (ready); #110764 and #111118 (Chiqun) touch the same doc and merge clean. Whichever lands second rebases its doc hunk; if they collide in substance, one is dropped.

#108984 rev 18: a client's own tier commits in every mode, so off live (shadow, off) its proposal_outcome reads the commit's result (committed, or dropped when another write superseded it); would_commit is left to an MD1 pick off live. Unit cases in the_proposal_outcome_names_what_the_record_holds.
